title: klaus.config.json
description: Klaus settings for one repo. Holds the names of secrets and logins, never their values.

outputs.description: One entry per design output. An output that is absent or has enabled false is never run.

inventory.description: Where the inventory script looks for components.

selection.description: Which components and screens the outputs receive. Every output uses the same selection.

componentGroups.description: Folders whose components are written. Empty or absent means every scanned folder.

newComponents.description: The rule for a component an output has not received before. all writes it, none leaves it for a person to add to componentGroups, min-usage writes it once it is used in at least minUsage places.

spendingCap.description: The most one run may spend on each output. Over the cap, the most-used components are written and the rest wait for the next run.

trigger.description: What starts a run. A one-off command always works besides this.

tagPattern.description: Git tag glob that marks a release. In release mode (a pushed tag) it may hold only letters, digits, . _ - and *, with no / and no **, so that the workflow's tag filter and the tag ruleset mean the same thing.
tagPattern.title: a git tag glob that does not start with a dash

cron.description: Five-field cron expression, required when mode is schedule.

approvedTagBypass.description: Release mode only. Who besides repository admins may bypass the tag ruleset that protects the release tags. Each entry was approved by name when Klaus was installed. A later render of the workflow refuses if the ruleset has gained anyone who is not listed here.

name.description: What the person approving it called it, for example the app's name.

onboarding.description: How the onboarding run (the baseline) writes and checks the purpose comments. The run shows the cost of these choices before it starts. A route named external means another agent does that part, such as Codex cloud for writing or a Cyrus session for checking: the run then writes that agent's briefs and verifies what comes back.

writer.description: Who writes the missing purpose comments, one call for each folder of components.

agent.description: Who the external route hands the briefs to, in words, for example Codex cloud (Terra).

checker.description: Who checks each written purpose against where its component is used. A different model family from the writer.

secrets.description: Names of environment variables the route reads. The writer's process never receives them.

usageSnippets.description: How many places a component is used the checker is shown.

agent.description: Who the external route hands the briefs to, in words, for example a Cyrus session on GLM.

dataBoundImports.description: Package names, or prefixes ending in a slash, whose use marks an app component as showing live data. Added to the built-in list.

docsDir.description: Where the duplicates list, the tickets and the decisions list are written.

modelName.description: a model name such as gpt-5.6-terra or z-ai/glm-5.3-flash

allOf.title: a model name such as gpt-5.6-terra or z-ai/glm-5.3-flash
a short plain description without special characters
a package name, or a prefix such as @clerk/

not.title: looks like a secret value. Give the name of an environment variable or a login instead

targetText.description: Where the output writes: a Vercel project, a design file key or URL, or a file path.

route.description: a route that starts with a slash and has no spaces

allOf.title: a route that starts with a slash and has no spaces
the name of an environment variable, upper case with underscores
the name of a login, lower case with dashes
a route name, lower case with dashes

route.description: How the output is reached, for example codex-relay. The adapter defines the names it accepts.

secrets.description: Names of environment variables the output reads. Values come from the environment at run time.

logins.description: Names of signed-in sessions the output relies on. The adapter checks them.

options.description: Settings only this output's adapter understands. The adapter checks the names and the values. A text value that looks like a secret is rejected.
